messages:
maria: Heads up — I'll be in Boston (Seaport) Tues–Thu next week. Any 'must eat' recs near the office? casual lunch + one good spot for dinner. also: quick grab near the convention center for a late flight?
kevin: Ooh nice. For casual lunch: Tatte if you want pastries/salad, Flour for sandwiches, and Row 34 for quick seafood.
sasha: If you're doing dinner and want something local, try Yvonne's for nicer spot or Uni for sushi. Both are walkable-ish from Seaport.
maria: sweet — any legendary bagel place or breakfast for early morning?
kevin: Mike's is touristy, but still good for a classic. If you want a local bagel vibe, try Blackbird Doughnuts (not a bagel but great). Also, Thinking Cup has solid coffee+pastries.
sasha: For quick grab near the convention center + airport run: Sweetgreen is on Seaport Blvd, or Duck Donuts if you want warm portable. Logan tip: if you have >45min, head to Legal Sea Foods (Terminal C has one).
maria: dinner recs noted. any late-night tacos/poke spots? arriving late Tues night.
kevin: For poke, Island Creek Oyster has bowls sometimes, but not true poke shop. There's a small poke place "Poke Perfect" in the Financial District — short Uber from Seaport.
sasha: Tacos: El Fuego or Taqueria El Barrio (food truck vibes) — check hours. Also, many places close early on weekdays, so call ahead if after 10pm.
maria: thanks! also — carrying a demo laptop, any quiet coffee spots with outlets for a 2hr sprint Wed morning?
kevin: Try District Hall cafe or Blue Bottle on Seaport — both have tables and plugs.
caterbot: FYI — free lunch next Friday in kitchen (sandwich spread) :sandwich: — not during your trip but marking calendar.
maria: perfect — saved. anyone else been recently and want to add any 'hidden gems'?
sasha: If you can get to the North End for dessert, Mike's Pastry cannoli > everything. Also, if you like ramen, Yume Wo Katare (line but worth it).
maria: ok this is great — gonna build a little itinerary. thanks y'all! :raised_hands:
